approachQuestion.prompt:
Inspect a Mirrored Log

A finite acyclic singly linked list contains integers. Return true exactly when the value sequence reads identically forwards and backwards. Before returning, restore every original link and value, including on false. Temporary next changes are allowed; allocate no replacement input nodes. Only head is supplied. Constraints: 0 <= n <= 200000.

Input: [4,9,9,4]. Output: true with original links restored.
Input: [4,9,6]. Output: false with original links restored. Empty input returns true.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Reverse the second half and return immediately on the first mismatch without restoration.
options.feedback: For [4,9,6,8] this leaves the second half reversed after returning false.

options.text: Check only the first and last values.
options.feedback: [4,9,6,4] has equal ends but unequal inner values.

options.text: Find the midpoint with two runners, iteratively reverse the second half, compare mirrored values while retaining a boolean, then reverse that half again and reconnect it before returning.
options.feedback: The comparisons cover mirrored positions; unconditional restoration preserves the original chain on either result.

options.text: Copy values into an array and compare symmetric entries without changing the input.
options.feedback: This is correct but stores avoidable copied values when reversible temporary changes are permitted.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-06-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.

options.explanation: This pair does not describe the fixed method. Midpoint search, comparison and two half reversals each traverse at most n nodes. Matching long lists force linear work. Fixed references and a boolean suffice because all reversals are iterative; output is one boolean.
